title: Japan for a Week
subtitle: Britain for Ever!
summary: A. M. Thompson, a London journalist and writer of musical plays, went to Japan with the theatre manager Robert Courtneidge to find “local colour” for a Japanese play to follow “The Arcadians”. The party crossed Germany and Russia and took the Trans-Siberian Railway, spent little more than a week in Japan, at Kyoto, Tokyo, Nikko, and the Inland Sea, and came home by Shanghai, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Colombo. The book gives no year.

The chapters on Japan describe tea-houses, temples, and trains and discuss labour, marriage, commercial honesty, politeness, and the English of Japanese signs. Those on China describe social conditions and the country’s awakening. The last chapters argue for the unity of the English-speaking peoples and warn of German power, ending with a letter from Lord Roberts. Seventeen photographs.
